title: Decrypt String from Alphabet to Integer Mapping
statement: `s` is an encoded message made only of digits and `#` characters. Every lowercase letter has a code: the letters `a` to `i` are written as the single digits `1` to `9`, and the letters `j` to `z` are written as the two-digit numbers `10` to `26` followed by a `#`. Decode `s` and return the string of lowercase letters it stands for. `s` is always a valid encoding, so it decodes in exactly one way.
constraints: s is a valid encoding, so exactly one decoding exists
notes:
## Intuition

The only ambiguity is whether a digit starts a one-digit code or a two-digit code. The `#` settles it: a two-digit code is always followed by `#`, so when reading left to right, a `#` two places ahead means the next two digits form one letter. Otherwise the current digit is a letter on its own. (Scanning from the right works too: a `#` there tells you to take the two digits before it.)

## Approach

1. Start at `i = 0` with an empty `letters` list.
2. If `s[i + 2]` exists and is `#`, the `code` is the two digits `s[i]s[i + 1]`; skip all three characters.
3. Otherwise the `code` is the single digit `s[i]`; skip one character.
4. Turn the code into a letter: code 1 is `a` (character 97), so the letter is character `96 + code`. Push it.
5. When `i` reaches the end, join `letters` and return the result.

## Example 1, step by step

`s = "10#11#12"`.

- `i = 0`: `s[2]` is `#`, so `code = 10`, letter `j`, `i = 3`.
- `i = 3`: `s[5]` is `#`, so `code = 11`, letter `k`, `i = 6`.
- `i = 6`: `s[8]` does not exist, so `code = 1`, letter `a`, `i = 7`.
- `i = 7`: `s[9]` does not exist, so `code = 2`, letter `b`, `i = 8`.

The scan ends, giving `"jkab"`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): each character is read a constant number of times.
- Space: O(n) for the output letters.

## Pitfalls

- Look **two** places ahead for `#`, not one: in `"1326#"` the `2` is followed by `6`, but `26#` is still one letter, and `1`, `3` are single letters before it.
- Check the bound `i + 2 < s.length` before reading `s[i + 2]`.
- Skip three characters after a `#` code so the `#` itself is not read as a digit.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `letters` | decoded letters so far |
| `i` | index of the next unread character in `s` |
| `code` | the number (1 to 26) of the letter being decoded |

narration.2: Collect the decoded letters here and join them at the end.
narration.3: Start reading at the first character.
narration.5: Keep decoding until every character has been used.
narration.7: A # two places ahead means the next two digits form one code from 10 to 26.
narration.8: Read those two digits as the code.
narration.11: Otherwise this digit alone is a code from 1 to 9.
narration.14: Code 1 is 'a' (character 97), so the letter is character 96 + code.
narration.16: Join the letters into the decoded string.
